turns.zh: 好。我们今天就来挽回一下，然后开始。今天我们有牛排，还要做 chimichurri 酱，那我们就开始吧。你能把欧芹递给我吗，我们可以开始切了。

turns.zh: 好。开始之前我也挺好奇的。你最初是带着一家叫 Remember All 的公司加入 YC 的，对吧？

turns.en: Correct.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.en: And even today, your company's called Reducto. And so I was wondering, are there any ties with Harry Potter?
turns.zh: 而且到今天，你的公司叫 Reducto。所以我想问，这跟《哈利·波特》有什么关联吗？

And we didn't know what we would pivot into specifically. There was this general idea of we'll make magical tools for developers, and we made a poll in a group chat saying here are the names and the domain names available for each.
turns.zh: 嗯，是的。故事是这样的：我们早就知道要从 Remember All 转型。进 YC 那天，我们就跟 Diana 说：“嘿，我们觉得这不是我们要做的方向。”当时我们也不知道具体会转到什么。大概的想法是，我们要为开发者做魔法般的工具，于是我们在群聊里发了个投票，列出每个名字和对应的可用域名。

turns.en: And this one, the name—
turns.zh: 然后这个名字——

turns.en: There were some horrible names in there. But yeah, I guess a lot has changed going from at that time it was long-horizon memory, or just memory for—
turns.zh: 里面有些名字特别糟糕。不过是啊，从那时候到现在变化很大，当时做的是长时程记忆，或者只是给……

turns.en: Memory for agents.
turns.zh: 给智能体的记忆。

ts.sec: The hard problem of reading documents

turns.en: And I guess to contextualize for the audience, do you want to provide some more breakdown of the core crux of the problem, and even maybe some history going from OCR to IDP and now today with VLMs and agents?
turns.zh: 为了给观众一点背景，你能不能再拆解一下这个问题的核心难点，甚至讲讲从 OCR 到 IDP、再到今天用视觉语言模型和智能体的历史？

turns.en: Yeah. So there are a few decades worth of companies that have worked on PDF processing. I met this guy that had worked on PDF processing longer than I've been alive. Quite literally, he worked on the original drivers for printers to print PDFs. The context in which people process documents is obviously very different though, in that these are just horizontal formats that a lot of people will use for cataloging information, and it's a unified set of data that people will use across enterprises. And so if you're going to have models do a lot of human work, it becomes really important that you have human-level fidelity when you're reading it.
turns.zh: 好。做 PDF 处理的公司已经有几十年的历史了。我遇到一个人，他做 PDF 处理的时间比我的年龄还长。毫不夸张，他做过让打印机打印 PDF 的原始驱动。不过人们处理文档的场景显然已经很不一样了，这些只是很多人用来归档信息的通用格式，是企业里通用的一套数据。所以如果你要让模型承担大量人类的工作，读取时的保真度达到人类水平就非常重要。

turns.en: Mh.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.en: And the tricky thing is—I hinted at this with the guy that worked on printer drivers—the original context for PDF as a file format was for printers to be faithful to the original, right? And so it wasn't really designed around this problem of agents are going to read it. And so we just got really, really deep in this rabbit hole of how can you read these documents the way that a human would.
turns.zh: 麻烦的地方在于——我在那位做打印机驱动的人那里提到过——PDF 作为一种文件格式，最初的场景是让打印机忠实还原原件，对吧？所以它并不是围绕“智能体要读它”这个问题设计的。于是我们就深深扎进了这个兔子洞：怎样才能像人一样读这些文档。

turns.en: Which is a really hard vision problem.
turns.zh: 这是个非常难的视觉问题。

turns.en: We liken it a lot to self-driving car research. There's been lane assist in cars for a long time, and it's a very different thing to say that your Waymo will drive fully end to end autonomously. That's the sort of bar that we want to get to with Reducto.
turns.zh: 我们常把它比作自动驾驶研究。车道辅助在车上已经存在很久了，但说你的 Waymo 能完全端到端自动驾驶，那是完全不同的事。这就是我们想在 Reducto 达到的标准。

turns.en: Gotcha. Okay, that makes sense. And I guess you guys are also an agentic platform. And I guess what does that generally entail beyond just being interactable with a lot of agents? Like do you see it also being a horizontal platform where you cover beyond processing and parsing to even editing, and having a node studio that clients can use?
turns.zh: 明白了。好，这说得通。我猜你们也是一个智能体式平台。那除了能跟很多智能体交互之外，这通常还意味着什么？你觉得它也会是一个横向平台吗，覆盖的不只是处理和解析，甚至还有编辑，并且有一个客户可以用的节点工作室？

turns.en: Yeah, the way to think about it is any sort of interaction that a model has with a document or unstructured files in general, we want Reducto to be the best way for that interaction to happen. That means reading the document, like parsing it, classifying that information, editing it. So much of human work is people reading from documents and writing into documents. That will take care of everything from extracting that data, reconciling it against other documents, and then getting the end output that they needed.
turns.zh: 对，可以这样理解：模型与文档、或广义上的非结构化文件之间的任何交互，我们都希望 Reducto 是完成这种交互的最佳方式。这包括读文档，比如解析、对信息分类、编辑。人类工作中很大一部分就是人从文档里读、再往文档里写。这会覆盖从提取数据、与其他文档核对，到最终拿到他们需要的输出的一切。

ts.sec: Model routing and the R1 model

turns.en: Gotcha. And do you guys consider routing? Because I read on the website that Reducto under the hood has 12-plus models. So what's the decision framework between choosing a cheaper model, let's say, versus a more expensive one for different tasks and files?
turns.zh: 明白了。你们会考虑路由吗？因为我在网站上看到 Reducto 底层有 12 个以上的模型。那针对不同任务和文件，在选更便宜的模型还是更贵的模型之间，决策框架是什么？

turns.en: So the tricky thing here is that a lot of it is ultimately a long-tail problem, right? And so you'll have a lot of pages that look like they're just text, and then every once in a while you'll have this really complex table, and you're not going to know exactly which page had that or anything like that. And so we started with this idea of, okay, we'll use a lot of smaller traditional CV models for the baseline, and then we'll use larger models for the really hard tasks. Over time, though, we've been able to have this pretty interesting approach to just the model architecture. We're going to announce this on Monday, which is our new in-house model. We're calling it R1, which is going to be able to do this end to end. So components of capturing the layout and all that, but also the last-mile corrections that you'd want to make sure that you're at as close to 100% as possible.
turns.zh: 这里的麻烦在于，这很大程度上最终是个长尾问题，对吧？你会有一大堆看起来只是纯文本的页面，然后偶尔冒出一个非常复杂的表格，而你并不知道哪一页会有这种东西。所以我们一开始的想法是，好，我们用很多更小的传统 CV 模型做基线，然后用更大的模型处理真正难的任务。不过随着时间推移，我们在模型架构上摸索出了一套挺有意思的做法。我们周一要发布这个，是我们新的自研模型，叫 R1，它能端到端完成这件事。既包括捕捉版面布局这些部分，也包括最后一公里的修正，确保尽可能接近 100%。

turns.en: Gotcha. Okay. That's pretty great. We could probably add the parsley now. I feel like just have it relatively chopped and then add the other elements. But yeah, I guess going on to what you mentioned with this new model, what is your framework or even mental models behind determining whether to own your intelligence versus rent it? Because last year, even though it was for a test, you had ROM OCR, which is built on top of the Qwen VLM. And with this new one coming out, it seems like you're maybe focusing on that and not depending on providers.
turns.zh: 明白了。好，这挺棒的。我们现在大概可以加欧芹了。我觉得把它切得差不多，然后再加其他配料。不过是啊，接着你提到的新模型，你们决定自研智能还是租用外部智能，背后的框架甚至心智模型是什么？因为去年，虽然只是测试，你们有个 ROM OCR，是建在 Qwen VLM 之上的。而随着这个新模型出来，看起来你们可能更专注自研，不再依赖供应商。

turns.en: Yeah. So our thesis, or like mandate for us as a team, is we want to be the best possible provider no matter what. Our customers don't think in terms of is Reducto using in-house models or something else. They just want incredible results. And so we don't want to look at it as is it in-house or not. The thing that's happened naturally over time is we care a lot about that sort of Pareto frontier of accuracy, cost and latency.
turns.zh: 对。我们的论点，或者说我们团队的任务，就是无论如何都要做最好的供应商。我们的客户不会去想 Reducto 用的是自研模型还是别的什么，他们只想要惊人的结果。所以我们不想用“是不是自研”来看这件事。随着时间自然发生的是，我们非常在意准确率、成本和延迟的那条帕累托前沿。

turns.en: Yeah. And we keep finding that if you are looking at a specific type of task, a post-trained model on that task outperforms on all three dimensions.
turns.zh: 是的。我们不断发现，如果你关注某一特定类型的任务，针对该任务进行后训练的模型在三个维度上都表现更优。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: And so our stack has shifted more and more towards in-house over time. There are still really horizontal tasks where a frontier foundation model makes sense, but that's limited in scope today.
turns.zh: 因此，我们的技术栈随着时间的推移越来越转向内部研发。仍然有一些非常通用的任务适合使用前沿基础模型，但如今范围有限。

turns.en: Great. Okay. And so for the next thing, do you want to cut the peaches so we can maybe get some grilled and I can... Do you want to take this new cutting board?
turns.zh: 太好了。好的。那么接下来，你想切桃子吗？这样我们可以烤一些，然后我可以……你要用这个新砧板吗？

turns.en: Yes. Thank you. And then I'll just take this so that I can.
turns.zh: 好的。谢谢。然后我拿这个，这样我就可以……

turns.en: Also, you weren't joking about it being distracting to talk while you cook.
turns.zh: 还有，你说做饭时聊天会分心，这不是开玩笑的。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: Yeah. And you guys recently launched the deep extract um and had the benchmark showing that the harness outperforms a lot of the base models. Yep. Um, and I guess how do you view the people come to you and say, "Why can't I just wait for these base models to get to the performance level and not need this harness and just use that compared to going to you guys?"
turns.zh: 是的。你们最近推出了 Deep Extract，并且有基准测试显示该工具链优于许多基础模型。是的。我想，你如何看待那些来找你说“为什么我不能等这些基础模型达到那个性能水平，不需要这个工具链，直接使用它们，而不是找你们？”的人？

turns.en: I think one of the most interesting things with the new launch was uh I don't know if you had a chance to read the blog, like we found this really weird trade-off between precision and recall. And so a lot of these specialized document processing platforms were worse than frontier models uh when you set uncap reasoning time.
turns.zh: 我认为这次新发布最有趣的事情之一是……我不知道你有没有机会读那篇博客，我们发现了一个非常奇怪的精确率和召回率之间的权衡。所以，许多这些专门的文档处理平台在你不限制推理时间时，表现比前沿模型更差。

turns.en: But the failure mode for the frontier models was on recall. So they were silently dropping rows um missing bits of context like those sorts of things.
turns.zh: 但前沿模型的失败模式在于召回率。所以它们会悄悄漏掉行，错过一些上下文之类的东西。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: And if you're thinking about your extraction layer just missing information altogether, that's the sort of loss pattern that you're just not going to find in production, right? like you don't know what you failed to extract in the first place. Um and those are the sorts of things where having a harness around making sure and auditing the results becomes really really important.
turns.zh: 如果你考虑你的提取层完全遗漏信息，那种损失模式在生产中你是找不到的，对吧？就像你根本不知道你一开始没能提取出什么。嗯，这些就是为什么有一个工具链来确保和审计结果变得非常非常重要。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: Um where I don't see it as either or like there are certainly tasks where a frontier model is great. But if you're looking for the most efficient tool for the task, you should probably specialize in terms of the task you're doing.
turns.zh: 嗯，我不认为这是二选一的问题，当然有些任务前沿模型很棒。但如果你在寻找针对该任务最高效的工具，你可能应该根据你正在做的任务进行专门化。

turns.en: Yeah. No, that makes sense. And I guess even for the announcement, you work with micro one to create benchmark. Yeah. Yeah. And I guess how do you think about um eval benchmarking tied with performance and even the concern of jagged performance for like benchmark benchmaxing y um across like the different tasks compared to like real world tasks.
turns.zh: 是的。不，这有道理。我想，即使对于公告，你们也与 Micro One 合作创建了基准测试。是的。是的。我想，你如何看待评估基准测试与性能的关联，甚至是对基准测试刷分的锯齿状性能的担忧，在不同任务之间与真实世界任务相比。

turns.en: So we obviously do a lot of benchmarking internally and something that's frustrating for me is benchmarks largely have become marketing material. M um everybody's number one on their own benchmark and so there's just this it becomes really really noisy really quickly. Um and so the reason why we worked with micro one was we just wanted this like clear line drawn of reducto is not choosing the documents. Redduck is not setting the ground truth. Product is not you know manipulating the results in any which way. Um just so there's this baseline of it's an independent benchmark. Um even that obviously is not perfect. I think at the end of the day, the thing that matters most is for people to try things on their own documents.
turns.zh: 所以显然我们在内部做了很多基准测试，让我感到沮丧的是，基准测试在很大程度上已经变成了营销材料。嗯，每个人在自己的基准测试上都是第一名，所以很快就变得非常非常嘈杂。嗯，所以我们与 Micro One 合作的原因是我们想要划清界限：Reducto 不选择文档。Reducto 不设定真实标准。产品不以任何方式操纵结果。嗯，只是为了有一个独立基准测试的基线。嗯，即使那样显然也不完美。我认为最终最重要的是让人们在自己的文档上尝试。

turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.en: Um but at least it gives like a directional sense for people to start thinking about these sorts of things which is all we care about.
turns.zh: 嗯，但至少它给人们一个方向感，开始思考这类事情，这就是我们关心的全部。

turns.en: Gotcha. And I guess tying in your recent launch R1 um does this indicate a change in how you guys will um do things? Is there anything interesting that you guys discovered while working on it?
turns.zh: 明白了。我想，结合你们最近的发布 R1，这是否表明你们做事方式的变化？你们在开发过程中有什么有趣的发现吗？

turns.en: Uh I think R1 is a really big step forward for us because for a while we had the sort of anchor points of reductive is going to be the most accurate thing that you've tried, right? Um and especially as we start doing larger volume work like today reducto processes a little over a billion pages every single month. Um and that number keeps changing really quickly. Yeah. it becomes really important to have that sort of perto frontier conversation of making this available for all sorts of different use cases. Um, the reason why I like R1 so much is it's not just an improvement from the lens of accuracy. It's also going to really simplify our pricing and the way that our customers get to adopt the product in production. So for a while we would have these multipliers if you were turning on aic features and things like that. Yeah, that's all going away. Um, our one is just you send us the documents, it it'll be less than the per page cost of our base models for better accuracy than our most accurate models.
turns.zh: 嗯，我认为 R1 对我们来说是一个巨大的进步，因为有一段时间我们的锚点是 Reducto 将是你尝试过的最准确的东西，对吧？嗯，特别是当我们开始做更大规模的工作时，比如今天 Reducto 每月处理超过十亿页。嗯，这个数字变化很快。是的。进行那种从平价到前沿的对话，使其适用于各种不同的用例，变得非常重要。嗯，我如此喜欢 R1 的原因是它不仅仅是准确性方面的改进。它还将真正简化我们的定价以及客户在生产中采用产品的方式。所以有一段时间，如果你开启 AI 功能之类的，我们会有这些乘数。是的，这些都消失了。嗯，我们的 R1 就是你发送文档给我们，每页成本将低于我们基础模型的每页成本，而准确性比我们最准确的模型更好。

turns.en: Oh wow. Okay. Yeah. So like the pricing is definitely a lot better um by far and away. Like it's multiples cheaper than where we used to be.
turns.zh: 哇。好的。是的。所以定价肯定好多了，远远好多了。就像比我们以前便宜好几倍。

turns.en: Gotcha. Dang. That is pretty exciting if you use Redducto at the scale that a lot of your customers do.
turns.zh: 明白了。哇。如果你像许多客户那样大规模使用 Reducto，那真是相当令人兴奋。

turns.en: Exactly. Yeah.
turns.zh: 没错。是的。

turns.en: Yeah. Which reminds me, you mentioned that a lot of your clients are in industries that have very low margin of error. Mhm. And I was kind of curious how you maybe think through um evaluating or even setting metrics for systems or even performance where let's say 99% accuracy may still not be enough if it fails on like the few use cases that um an enterprise really needs in let's say healthcare or a very low margin error industry. Like asymmetrical um use cases. How do you like think through evaluating that and considering that?
turns.zh: 是的。这让我想起，你提到你的许多客户所在的行业容错率非常低。嗯。我有点好奇你如何思考评估甚至为系统或性能设定指标，比如 99% 的准确率可能仍然不够，如果它在企业真正需要的少数用例上失败，比如在医疗保健或容错率非常低的行业。就像不对称的用例。你如何思考评估和考虑这一点？

turns.en: So the first order problem is ideally our first pass should be as accurate as possible. Um and obviously that's where a lot of our head space is. But the second thing is there's never going to be a line for truly perfect. Like even if you get really really good at reading what's on the page, maybe you have ambiguity or things like that. Um and so traceability becomes really important. like being able to know where something was extracted from, being able to say uh exactly what a human should look at if they're reviewing it. Um and also having things like accurate confidence scoring so they know when to look at a certain thing. Um that becomes really really important if you're going to do something like healthcare document workflows. Yeah. Um and so internally when we do benchmarks, we don't only measure ourselves on extraction accuracy. We say like of the things that weren't perfect, how reliably could we escalate to a human that this is not perfect? All of that kind of stuff really matters too.
turns.zh: 所以首要问题是，理想情况下我们的第一遍应该尽可能准确。嗯，显然这是我们很多精力所在。但第二件事是，永远不会有真正完美的界限。就像即使你非常非常擅长阅读页面上的内容，也许会有歧义之类的东西。嗯，所以可追溯性变得非常重要。比如能够知道某物是从哪里提取的，能够说出如果人工审核时应该看什么。嗯，还有准确的置信度评分，这样他们知道何时该查看某个东西。嗯，如果你要做医疗文档工作流之类的事情，那变得非常非常重要。是的。嗯，所以在内部做基准测试时，我们不仅衡量提取准确性。我们说，在那些不完美的事情中，我们能多可靠地升级给人类说这不完美？所有这些事情也很重要。

turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好的。

turns.en: And so do you I guess keep track of all the hardest failure instances and then put that in like a data set that you could run to make sure that there are no regressions with like your harnesses?
turns.zh: 那么，你们会跟踪所有最难的失败实例，然后把它放进一个数据集里运行，以确保你们的测试框架没有回归吗？

consensus.en: Document parsing must achieve human-level fidelity because agents will read PDFs for critical enterprise work.
consensus.zh: 文档解析必须达到人类级别的保真度，因为智能体将读取 PDF 用于关键的企业工作。

consensus.en: Post-trained specialized models outperform frontier models on accuracy, cost, and latency for specific tasks.
consensus.zh: 针对特定任务进行后训练的专用模型在准确性、成本和延迟上优于前沿模型。

consensus.en: Continuous evaluation and failure-mode analysis are key to handling long-tail document processing at scale.
consensus.zh: 持续评估和故障模式分析是在规模上处理长尾文档的关键。

consensus.en: Hiring for obsession with craft and rigor is more important than specific prior experience.
consensus.zh: 招聘时看重对技艺的痴迷和严谨，比特定过往经验更重要。

consensus.en: Horizontal platforms that master document primitives can serve multiple industries better than vertical solutions.
consensus.zh: 掌握文档基元的水平平台比垂直解决方案能更好地服务多个行业。

consensus.en: The next wave of white-collar automation requires editing and writing into documents, not just extraction.
consensus.zh: 下一波白领自动化需要编辑和写入文档，而不仅仅是提取。

contrarian.en: Benchmarks have largely become marketing material; independent benchmarks and real-world testing matter most.
contrarian.zh: 基准测试在很大程度上已成为营销材料；独立基准和真实世界测试最重要。

contrarian.en: Frontier models silently drop information (recall failures), which is worse than precision issues in production.
contrarian.zh: 前沿模型会静默丢失信息（召回失败），这比生产中的精确度问题更糟糕。

contrarian.en: Model intelligence is no longer the biggest bottleneck; data fragmentation and context aggregation are.
contrarian.zh: 模型智能不再是最大瓶颈；数据碎片化和上下文聚合才是。

contrarian.en: In-house specialized models can be cheaper and more accurate than renting frontier models for document tasks.
contrarian.zh: 对于文档任务，内部专用模型可能比租用前沿模型更便宜且更准确。

contrarian.en: Competitive markets are meritocratic and good; companies must rise to the challenge rather than avoid competition.
contrarian.zh: 竞争市场是精英主义的且有益的；公司必须迎接挑战而不是回避竞争。

contrarian.en: Founders should not force top-down AI adoption; lead by example and let natural enthusiasm drive usage.
contrarian.zh: 创始人不应强制自上而下地采用 AI；以身作则，让自然热情驱动使用。
